text:
jamal: Heads-up — proposal to keep on-prem seed caches for 30 days and prune stale bundles automatically. Reason: limited storage on customer appliances and operator UX.

alex: +1 on pruning but worried about rollback window. If we prune too aggressively, rollbacks for past 90 days will fail.

priya: Could we keep metadata + small index for 90d and only store full blobs for 30d? Index size tiny.

maria: That matches what we discussed in the runtime rfc — a two-tier retention. But we need operator APIs to rehydrate from mirrors.

jamal: Exactly. Sketch:
```
retention:
  index_days: 90
  blob_days: 30
  keep_tags: [canary, latest]
```

alex: How do we reconcile with airgap customers that receive seed media? They might not have mirrors.

priya: For seed media, operator will need a 'retain-local' flag during seed ingestion. Default false, can be true for compliance.

ops-bot: deploy-check: airflow: no changes to installer mock. flagged for follow-up.

maria: Also consider GC coordination across sidecar/seed-swap so operator doesn't delete a blob still referenced by an activation window.

jamal: Plan: RFC follow-up to add (1) index-only retention, (2) operator rehydrate API, (3) seed-ingest retain flag, (4) GC lease extension endpoint. Will draft.

alex: +1. Add a CLI 'packman reprobe --missing' to surface missing payloads during rollout.

priya: Small UX note: default retention policy should be conservative; make it opt-in for aggressive pruning.

maria: Also add telemetry: counts of pruned bytes, last_rehydrate_time for audit.

dev-bot: Reminder — please add unit tests for packman gc and integration test with offline seed. :robot_face:

jamal: I'll open the RFC draft today and tag core-ops. Thanks all :rocket:
